STEP 1 - Scene: A small portion of cooked broccoli florets (appears roasted or charred) on a white square plate, photographed from above at a near top-down angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is roughly 20 cm across (similar to a side plate). Area ≈ 20 × 20 × ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 340 cm²; I use 314 cm² (equivalent circle of ~20 cm diameter).

STEP 3 - Items: Charred/roasted broccoli florets and small stem pieces (about 5-6 pieces, with a few small crumbs). No visible oil or sauce pooling.

STEP 4 - Area: Broccoli pieces together cover roughly 12% of the plate area (about 38 cm²).

STEP 5 - Volume: Pile height is low, around 1.5-2 cm for the florets. 38 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 57 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cut vegetable pieces, bulk density ~0.5-0.6 g/ml. 57 ml × 0.55 ≈ 31 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked broccoli ≈ 35 kcal/100 g (roasted, dry-ish, slightly higher per gram possibly). 31 g × 35 kcal/100 g ≈ 11 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A few small florets and stem pieces on a 20 cm plate should weigh tens of grams, not hundreds. About 30 g and ~11 kcal is plausible for what is visible.
